title: Tools of good works (Rule 4)
hook: a long list of tools, ending: never despair of God's mercy
tomorrow: why would Benedict ration even the good words?

segments.voice: A school of the Lord's service: Benedict's Rule calls itself a little rule for beginners, narrow at the door and wide inside. And every school hands out equipment.

Plenty of notes apps hold a list called something like be a better person: drink water, call Grandma, stop scrolling at midnight. Chapter four of Benedict's Rule is that list, for a monastery, and he calls the items tools. Love the Lord God with all your heart. Visit the sick. Bury the dead. Don't return evil for evil. Love your enemies. Don't be a grumbler. Keep death daily before your eyes. Tool after tool. And the one he saves for last is the tool for when every other one has slipped out of your hand: never despair of God's mercy.
screen: `THE BE-A-BETTER-PERSON LIST.` → `TOOL AFTER TOOL.` → `THE LAST ONE: MERCY.`

segments.voice: Benedict calls them the instruments of good works, the tools of the spiritual craft. A carpenter doesn't use every tool at once; she picks up the one the job needs. Some come straight from the Gospels: love God, and love your neighbor as yourself. Some are small: don't love much talking, make peace with an opponent before the sun goes down. And the workshop, he says, is the monastery, and staying put in one community. Now, Christians have a real conversation about lists like this. One side says a rule of life is how faith becomes a life. Without tools, love stays a feeling; with them, it gets hands. That's why some Christians, monks and others, keep a rule of life. The other side worries that a list turns into a scorecard. They hear Paul: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast." A checklist, they say, can crowd out grace, and leave a person either proud or crushed. Here's what's worth telling a friend: Benedict's last tool sits right where those two views meet. The list is real work, and it ends on a gift. Anyone who picks it up will drop something. The last tool keeps them from throwing the whole toolbox away.
screen: `TOOLS OF THE SPIRITUAL CRAFT.` · `ONE VIEW: TOOLS GIVE LOVE HANDS.` · `THE OTHER: LISTS CROWD OUT GRACE.` · `THE LAST TOOL IS A GIFT.` · then, large: `NEVER DESPAIR OF GOD'S MERCY.`

segments.voice: Pick one tool from the list: visit the sick, make peace before sundown, don't grumble. Name one place this week it would help, name what usually gets in the way, and plan the moment you'll reach for it. If you pray, you can end on Benedict's last tool: never despair of God's mercy.
Tools of good works. Benedict's list of small, practical instruments for a life with God, ending with mercy.
Your line: never despair of God's mercy. It's the tool Benedict left for last, for the days the others slip. See you tomorrow.
